content.description: Illustration showing accumulator pistons being removed using compressed air through holes in the transmission case

content.text: 18. COVER PISTON WITH A RAG AND REMOVE ACCUMULATOR PISTONS AND SPRINGS

WARNING: Keep your hand away. Position a rag to catch each piston. Using low-pressure compressed air (1 kg/cm², 14 psi or 98 kPa; max.), pop each piston into the rag. Force air into the holes shown, and remove the pistons and springs.

content.description: Illustration showing removal of parking lock rod from transmission case

content.text: 20. REMOVE SPRING, PIVOT PIN AND PARKING LOCK PAWL

content.description: Illustration showing removal of manual lever shaft using hammer and punch to drive out pin and slide shaft from detent plate

content.text: 21. IF NECESSARY, REMOVE MANUAL LEVER SHAFT

items: (a) Using a hammer and screwdriver, pry and shift the collar.
(b) Using a hammer and punch, drive out the pin.
(c) Slide the shaft out case and remove the detent plate.

content.description: Illustration showing transmission case being placed on a cylindrical stand

content.text: Place the transmission on a cylindrical stand for more efficient work.
CAUTION: Place shop rags between the case and stand to avoid damaging the case.

content.description: Illustration showing SST tool placement on transmission case to measure distance between top of case and clutch drum. Includes detail view of SST positioning

content.text: 23. MEASURE DISTANCE BETWEEN TOP OF CASE AND CLUTCH DRUM
Set SST on the case as shown in the figure.
Make a note of the finding for reassembly.
